title: Reading · Seq 3 Structure of research articles (IMRaD)

questions.explanation: An acronym from the four main sections of a paper: Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion.

questions.stem: Why is the IMRaD format used?
options: It allows authors to skip the Methods section
It is the structure of many journals, a universal standard
It presents information in a logical sequence (question → methods → results → implications)
It lets readers find specific information without reading the whole paper
questions.explanation: Logical sequence, quick access to information, universal standard in research communication.

questions.stem: According to the lecture, which section would a statistician typically go to first?
questions.explanation: "A statistician might go straight to the Methods, while a clinician may jump to the Results and Discussion."

questions.stem: Match the IMRaD section to the question it answers:
options: Introduction — Why was this study done?
Methods — How was the study done?
Results — What do the findings mean?
questions.explanation: Results = What did you find? Discussion = What do the findings mean? (Table 2.1)

questions.stem: The Introduction of a research article contains:
options: The statistical analysis of the data
questions.explanation: Statistical analysis is part of the Results.

options: It is the detailed "recipe" of the study
It states the study design (e.g. RCT, cohort)
It must be replicable by others
questions.explanation: Interpretation belongs to the Discussion. Methods = design, participants, materials, procedures — replicable.

options: It presents all data and findings objectively
Key results are often shown in tables, graphs and charts
It interprets the results and compares them with the literature
questions.explanation: Table 2.1: "No interpretation here" — interpretation is in the Discussion.

options: The detailed list of participants and materials
How findings fit with existing knowledge
questions.explanation: Participants and materials are in the Methods. Discussion: interpretation, fit with knowledge, limitations, implications.

questions.stem: A sentence such as "Our results suggest that…" or "This is the first study to show…" belongs to:
questions.explanation: Formative Part 1, item 5: interpretive statements belong to the Discussion.

questions.stem: "Describes how the study was conducted, including sample size and procedures" corresponds to:
Mapping a research article helps by:
options: Identifying the research question, methods and key results
Replacing the need to read the Methods
Supporting critical evaluation of the study's quality and relevance
questions.explanation: Fourth benefit: preparing readers to apply findings in practice or further research.

questions.stem: Tools for mapping a research article cited by the lecture:
questions.explanation: Tables, mind maps, flowcharts or digital templates.

questions.stem: When mapping the Discussion, the questions to ask include:
options: Who participated and what intervention was used?
questions.explanation: "Who participated, what intervention?" is asked when mapping the Methods.

questions.stem: In the "Hand Washing Training for Posyandu Cadres" study (Susila et al., 2025):
options: The intervention used counseling, a PowerPoint presentation and printed brochures
It was a randomized controlled trial of 1,200 students
The health problem was diarrhea and typhoid in Indonesian children
questions.explanation: It was a community service activity (educational intervention). The 1,200-student RCT is the formative excerpt.

questions.stem: The implied limitations of the hand-washing training study are:
options: No pre- and post-tests or long-term follow-up mentioned

questions.stem: According to the WHO data cited in the Discussion, hand washing with soap reduces:
In the formative excerpt (school hand hygiene study), which statements are correct?
options: The primary outcome was hand-washing technique scores
The design was a randomized controlled trial
The main result was a 30% reduction in respiratory-illness absences
The limitation/next step is that long-term effects require further study
questions.explanation: Primary outcome = number of sick days reported. RCT in 10 schools (n=1,200) over 12 weeks.
